questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which of these does NOT belong with the others about Romeo and Juliet's author and context?
options: William Shakespeare wrote the play
The play is set in Verona, Italy
The play was written in the 20th century
The play is classified as a tragedy
questions.answer: The play was written in the 20th century
questions.why: Shakespeare wrote in the late 16th century, not the 20th century. The other three facts are accurate features of the play's authorship, setting, and genre.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Match each technique in Romeo and Juliet to its example: 1) Oxymoron, 2) Metaphor, 3) Dramatic irony, 4) Foreshadowing. A) 'Loving hate'. B) Juliet is the sun. C) Audience knows Juliet is alive but Romeo doesn't. D) The Prologue revealing the lovers' fate.
questions.why: Oxymoron pairs contradictory words like 'loving hate', metaphor directly compares Juliet to the sun, dramatic irony is when the audience knows more than a character, and foreshadowing hints at future events like the Prologue does.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A student explains asexual reproduction using this worked argument. Which step is WRONG? Step 1: Asexual reproduction involves only one parent. Step 2: Offspring produced asexually are genetically identical to the parent. Step 3: Identical twins in humans are an example of asexual reproduction. Step 4: Bacteria splitting by binary fission is an example of asexual reproduction.
options: Step 1: Asexual reproduction involves only one parent
Step 2: Offspring produced asexually are genetically identical to the parent
Step 3: Identical twins in humans are an example of asexual reproduction
Step 4: Bacteria splitting by binary fission is an example of asexual reproduction
questions.answer: Step 3: Identical twins in humans are an example of asexual reproduction
questions.why: Identical twins form when a fertilised egg (from sexual reproduction) splits in two — the reproduction that created them was still sexual, so twins are not an example of asexual reproduction.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which statement about the fall of Rome and the medieval era that followed is FALSE?
options: The Western Roman Empire is generally dated as falling in 476 CE
Central political authority broke down across much of Western Europe after Rome fell
Western Europe had fully organised national governments again within a few years of Rome's fall
The Catholic Church became a major unifying power in Europe after Rome's collapse
questions.answer: Western Europe had fully organised national governments again within a few years of Rome's fall
questions.why: After Rome fell, Western Europe fragmented into small, weak, local territories for centuries — organised nation-states did not reappear quickly, which is why the period is often called the 'Dark Ages' in political terms.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Put these levels of the feudal pyramid in order from HIGHEST to LOWEST power: Peasants (serfs), King, Knights, Lords/Nobles.
options: King, Lords/Nobles, Knights, Peasants (serfs)
King, Knights, Lords/Nobles, Peasants (serfs)
Lords/Nobles, King, Knights, Peasants (serfs)
King, Lords/Nobles, Peasants (serfs), Knights
questions.why: The feudal pyramid ran King at the top, then Lords/Nobles who held land from the king, then Knights who served the lords, then Peasants (serfs) at the bottom who worked the land.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In Romeo and Juliet, which line best captures the play's theme of love intertwined with hate?
options: 'My only love sprung from my only hate'
'A plague o' both your houses'
'Wisely and slow; they stumble that run fast'
'These violent delights have violent ends'
questions.answer: 'My only love sprung from my only hate'
questions.why: This line directly fuses love and hate in one phrase, capturing Juliet's realisation that she loves someone from her family's enemy house — the clearest expression of the theme.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Match each variable type to its correct example from an experiment testing how light intensity affects plant growth: 1) Independent variable, 2) Dependent variable, 3) Controlled variable. A) Amount of water given to each plant. B) Light intensity provided to each plant. C) Height of the plant after two weeks.
questions.why: The independent variable is what you deliberately change (light intensity), the dependent variable is what you measure as a result (plant height), and the controlled variable is kept the same throughout (water amount).

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Put these Crusades-related events in chronological order: Jerusalem is captured by the First Crusade, The First Crusade is launched, Crusader states are eventually lost, Trade links between Europe and the Middle East expand.
options: The First Crusade is launched, Jerusalem is captured by the First Crusade, Trade links between Europe and the Middle East expand, Crusader states are eventually lost
The First Crusade is launched, Crusader states are eventually lost, Jerusalem is captured by the First Crusade, Trade links between Europe and the Middle East expand
Jerusalem is captured by the First Crusade, The First Crusade is launched, Trade links between Europe and the Middle East expand, Crusader states are eventually lost
The First Crusade is launched, Jerusalem is captured by the First Crusade, Crusader states are eventually lost, Trade links between Europe and the Middle East expand
questions.answer: The First Crusade is launched, Jerusalem is captured by the First Crusade, Trade links between Europe and the Middle East expand, Crusader states are eventually lost
questions.why: The Crusade was launched first, then Jerusalem was captured in 1099, trade and cultural exchange grew during the crusader states' existence, and the states were eventually lost afterward — the lasting trade effects are why historians see it as significant beyond the military outcome.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which statement about William Shakespeare and the writing of Romeo and Juliet is FALSE?
options: Shakespeare wrote Romeo and Juliet in the late 1590s, drawing on earlier Italian and English poems about doomed lovers.
Shakespeare invented the entire plot of Romeo and Juliet himself, with no earlier versions of the story existing before his play.
Shakespeare's plays were performed by his company at the Globe Theatre in London for a mixed audience of nobles and commoners.
Shakespeare wrote most of his plays, including Romeo and Juliet, using a mix of blank verse and prose rather than only prose.
questions.answer: Shakespeare invented the entire plot of Romeo and Juliet himself, with no earlier versions of the story existing before his play.
questions.why: Shakespeare actually based Romeo and Juliet on existing sources, especially Arthur Brooke's 1562 narrative poem 'The Tragical History of Romeus and Juliet' — he adapted and improved an existing story rather than inventing it from nothing. This is a common misconception that overstates Shakespeare's originality.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which of these does NOT belong as an example of Shakespeare's use of dramatic technique in Romeo and Juliet?
options: Juliet comparing Romeo to the sun as a metaphor
The Prologue using a sonnet form to foreshadow events
The audience knowing Juliet is alive while Romeo believes she is dead
The Nurse listing the ingredients of a herbal remedy in exact detail
questions.answer: The Nurse listing the ingredients of a herbal remedy in exact detail
questions.why: This is a fabricated detail with no real dramatic technique purpose, unlike metaphor, foreshadowing, and dramatic irony, which are genuine techniques Shakespeare uses throughout the play.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A student explains why fungi reproduction is misunderstood using this worked argument. Which step is WRONG? Step 1: Some fungi, like mushrooms, can reproduce using spores without a mate. Step 2: This spore production without a mate is a form of asexual reproduction. Step 3: Therefore, all fungi can only reproduce asexually and never sexually. Step 4: In fact, many fungi can also reproduce sexually by combining genetic material from two individuals.
options: Step 1: Some fungi, like mushrooms, can reproduce using spores without a mate
Step 2: This spore production without a mate is a form of asexual reproduction
Step 3: Therefore, all fungi can only reproduce asexually and never sexually
Step 4: In fact, many fungi can also reproduce sexually by combining genetic material from two individuals
questions.answer: Step 3: Therefore, all fungi can only reproduce asexually and never sexually
questions.why: Many fungi are capable of both asexual and sexual reproduction, so it's wrong to conclude they can only reproduce one way — mushrooms often use spores asexually but can also reproduce sexually under certain conditions.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A classmate says studying the Crusades is a waste of time because they were fought over religion, and 'nobody cares about religious wars anymore.' Explain, using your own reasoning and at least one specific long-term effect, why the Crusades still matter to study today even though modern society is more secular.
